summary: A local news piece announces a series of autumn cultural festivals running from September 3rd to November, held in parks, squares and community centers across the city. Events include the Harvest Moon Festival, EuroFest, the Global Rhythms Festival, The Little Global Village, Diwali, and the Day of the Dead Fiesta. Each is led by named organizers and offers food, workshops, performances and hands-on activities meant to celebrate diversity and bring residents together.
one_line: The community will host autumn cultural festivals from September to November, from Harvest Moon to Diwali and Day of the Dead, celebrating diverse traditions.
key_facts: The series of cultural festivals begins September 3rd and runs until November, in parks, squares and community centers.

The Harvest Moon Festival starts at Lunar Park on September 3rd from 2 PM until midnight, led by organizer Jamie Chen, and features East Asian traditional dances, martial arts, calligraphy workshops and a community potluck with mooncakes and regional teas.

EuroFest is scheduled for September 16-17th 2023 at Heritage Plaza, planned by Martin and Isabella Hofmann as a two-day European Village Fair with food stalls, workshops and a traditional maypole dance.
The EuroFest section is headed 'EuroFest 2018' although the dates given are in 2023.
EuroFest includes cultural crafts workshops in pottery-making, weaving and glassblowing.
The Global Rhythms Festival is on October 8th 2023 at Central Park Amphitheater, curated by choreographer Carlos Garcia, with music and dance from Africa, South America and the Caribbean.
Global Rhythms workshops cover salsa, samba, Afrobeat and Bollywood dance, plus percussion workshops for drumming.
The Little Global Village runs October 21-22nd 2023 at the Community Recreation Center, organized by educator Sarah Kim, with storytelling, arts and crafts and interactive games for families.
Sarah Kim says, "Children learn best through play."
Diwali will be celebrated on November 4th 2023 on the riverfront with thousands of lanterns and fireworks, coordinated by Priya Singh, and includes a community rangoli competition.
The Day of the Dead Fiesta is on November 2, 2023, organized by Maria Lopez and Diego Ramirez of Angelica Park's Latino Cultural Committee.
The Day of the Dead Fiesta invites people to contribute photographs and mementos to a public ofrenda, make sugar skulls and watch folk dancing.
The article describes the Day of the Dead Fiesta as rounding off the season, although it is dated November 2, before the November 4th Diwali event.
